clue.text: Partner in punt next to bank

indicators.note: next to says one piece sits directly beside the other in the answer

blocks.note: a river bank is one side of the water
in rugby a punt is a kick from the hands

explanation.surface: Someone shares a punt drifting beside the riverbank, like a lazy Cambridge afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punt' suggests the flat-bottomed boat, but it is the rugby kick; the bank piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is a close companion or assistant, the junior figure in a working pair.

clue.text: Fiction with foundation in Irish emblem

blocks.note: a sham is a pretence, something made up
rock is the bedrock a building rests on, joined on after

explanation.surface: A story said to be built on an Irish symbol, like a legend about a national badge.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the foundation naturally goes underneath, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-leaved clover is the national plant badge of Ireland, worn on Saint Patrick's Day.

clue.text: Problem raised in middle of eating fruit? Not on

indicators.note: not tells us to drop the two letters of the little word that follows it from the fruit
something eating another takes it inside itself
in a down entry, raising the letters means reading them from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: amid means in the middle of
a melon is a fruit
the word itself, removed from the fruit

explanation.surface: Someone mid-meal finds a dubious fruit and wonders whether to keep eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In middle of' is not placement here but a word in its own right, the one that does the eating; the whole build is then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult choice between two options, a predicament or awkward problem.

clue.text: Range over unknown area in country

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece on top of the rest

blocks.note: ken is one's range of knowledge or sight
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z
standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A mountain range stands over some unmapped region of a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like mountains, but here it is ken, the scope of what one knows.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenya is an East African nation, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Wild ranter during strike gives publicity to topical events

indicators.note: wild letters run out of control, out of their proper order
during means within, so the jumbled letters sit inside the blow

blocks.note: to cuff is to strike with the hand; it holds the jumble
the letters to be mixed
airs means makes public, broadcasts

explanation.surface: A furious ranter during an industrial strike is broadcasting news of the dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests a walkout, but it is a slap, CUFF, with the shuffled ranter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Current affairs is the stock phrase for news and political matters of the moment, things happening now.

clue.text: Loose plug split

blocks.note: a plug is a piece of promotion, an advert
a rift is a split or break

explanation.surface: An electrical plug has come apart and is hanging loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' suggests a socket or bath plug, but it is promotion, as in plugging a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adrift is floating free, unmoored and unattached, which is what loose means here.

clue.text: Group of people in rising uttered verbal attacks

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising letters are read from the bottom up
in places the group inside the other word

blocks.note: said means uttered; it is turned upward and holds the group
a tribe is a group of people

explanation.surface: A rebellious community rises up and voices its angry complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reads like an uprising, but it turns the word for uttered upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter, forceful spoken or written denunciation, a sustained tirade against someone.

clue.text: Examine bug restricting power

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the creature holds the letter inside it

blocks.note: a bug is an insect
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Checking a listening device that limits electricity use, like a sweep for hidden equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' suggests a hidden microphone or a software fault, but it is simply an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to look closely at something in order to check its condition, which is to examine it.

clue.text: Story not without heart and skill

indicators.note: without heart means the central letter of the short word is removed

blocks.note: a tale is a story
taken as written, then its middle letter goes

explanation.surface: A story that lacks emotional depth and craft, like a harsh review.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'not' is a piece of the wordplay, not a negative: NOT loses its O.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent is a natural aptitude or gift for doing something well, a synonym of skill.

clue.text: Glowing broadcast cons the shopper

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are strewn in a new order

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dazzling television advert tricks the consumer into buying.
explanation.definitionFit: Phosphorescent things give off light without burning, continuing to shine after exposure, so they are luminous.

clue.text: Section of vital links wiped out

indicators.note: a section of the phrase means a run of consecutive letters taken from inside it

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Part of a crucial chain or network has been destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: All in is informal for exhausted, utterly worn out, the same as being wiped out after effort.

clue.text: Catches in actual practice

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the second

blocks.note: real means actual
to catch a remark is to hear it

explanation.surface: A fielder takes catches during real training, cricket nets rather than a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catches' suggests fielding, but it is hearing, as in catching what someone said.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a trial run of a performance, practice before the real thing.

clue.text: Odd game disrupted search

indicators.note: disrupted letters have been thrown into disorder

blocks.note: rum is an old-fashioned word for odd or strange
the letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: A strange match was interrupted, then players had to hunt for something.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum, meaning peculiar, is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To rummage is to hunt through things untidily, turning them over while looking for something.

clue.text: One qualified to operate system initially and press ahead

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the preceding word is used

blocks.note: the first letter of this word
to urge on is to press forward

explanation.surface: Someone trained to run a system first, then push forward with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operate' looks like running machinery, but the definition means operating on patients.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a doctor licensed to perform operations, so the definition's pun on operate fits.

clue.text: Show impatience in talk about politician with silly hat, I bet

indicators.note: silly words are scrambled, put into a foolish order
about means around, so the chat surrounds everything else

blocks.note: chat is talk; it wraps round the rest
Member of Parliament
the letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: Someone bets that a politician will turn up in a ridiculous hat during a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma in 'hat, I bet' is only surface punctuation; the talk word wraps round everything that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ at the bit is the idiom, from a restless horse biting its bit, for being eager and impatient.

clue.text: Simple obligation, guarding against being mournful

indicators.note: guarding means holding protectively inside

blocks.note: plain means simple
a tie is a binding obligation
v for versus, against

explanation.surface: A straightforward duty, resisted, leaves someone feeling sorrowful.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintive sound or look expresses sadness, melancholy and complaint, so it is mournful.

clue.text: Sweet daughter after attention surrounded by support

indicators.note: after places the letter for daughter behind the word for attention
surrounded by means held inside the support word

blocks.note: a prop is a support
to give ear is to pay attention
standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A lovely daughter, after being noticed, is held up by her family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective describing the daughter, but it is a noun: the confection.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear drop is a boiled confection with a pear-like flavour, a classic British sweet.

clue.text: Saint provides charter for county

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for saint
affords means provides
to charter a boat or plane is to hire it

explanation.surface: A saint grants a royal charter to a county, like a medieval founding document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charter' suggests a founding document, but it is the verb meaning rent. Staffordshire is a county in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffordshire is an English shire in the West Midlands, so it is an example of a county.

clue.text: Elastic band round plant? On the contrary

indicators.note: round says one piece goes around the other
on the contrary flips the stated relation, so the second piece goes around the first instead

blocks.note: a plant is a spy placed inside an organisation
a ring is a band, as on a finger

explanation.surface: A rubber band wrapped round a plant stem, as gardeners tie up seedlings.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, band goes round plant; 'On the contrary' swaps that, so plant goes round band. 'Plant' is a mole, not greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Something springy bounces back into shape when pressed, which is what being elastic means.

clue.text: Detailed description's first suppressed by useless hotel

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the possessive word is taken
suppressed by means held down inside the next word

blocks.note: inept means useless or incompetent
the first letter of this word
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A shoddy hotel hides the opening of a detailed review, like a cover-up.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-depth study is thorough and comprehensive, examining every aspect, so it is fully detailed.

clue.text: Empty areas in resort dry up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a spa is a health resort
sec is the wine term for dry

explanation.surface: Holiday destinations have deserted patches once the weather dries everything out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry up' suggests running out, but dry is the wine word, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaces are gaps or unoccupied stretches, places with nothing in them, so they are empty areas.

clue.text: Fierce aquatic creature? Old man, to catch one, worked hard

indicators.note: to catch means to hold the following pieces inside

blocks.note: pa is a father, one's old man
I is the Roman numeral one
to run a business is to work or manage it
H for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An elderly angler toils hard to land a single dangerous fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The old man catches not just 'one' but everything after it: the outer letters hold the rest of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The piranha is a South American river fish famous for its razor teeth and ferocious feeding.

clue.text: Defamation put down in sermon? Not half

indicators.note: not half means only half the word is kept and the rest dropped
in places the first piece inside the shortened word

blocks.note: taken as written; its first half is kept
to land a plane is to put it down

explanation.surface: A preacher's sermon contains a disparaging remark, though not half as harsh as feared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' suggests an insult, fitting the definition, but it means touching down.
explanation.definitionFit: Slander is the spoken form of defamation, false statements that damage someone's reputation.

clue.text: Advantage when prepared

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
set means ready or prepared

explanation.surface: Being ready gives you an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or resource, something that gives benefit or an edge.

clue.text: Terribly egocentric, having no time for hotel employee

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters end up in disorder
having no time means the letter for time is taken out

blocks.note: the letters to be used
T is the abbreviation for time, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A self-absorbed guest is too busy to bother with the hotel staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the T out of egocentric and shuffle the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A concierge is the hotel staff member who helps guests with bookings, directions and arrangements.

clue.text: Smashing odd bits of sculpted alabaster finally

indicators.note: odd bits are the letters in the first, third, fifth and seventh places
finally means only the closing letter of the stone word

blocks.note: letters one, three, five and seven
its final letter

explanation.surface: Pieces of a carved stone statue are being broken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' fits the broken sculpture, but it is British slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashing and super are both informal British words of praise meaning wonderful or excellent.

clue.text: Farmyard enclosure was first to be designed

blocks.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
to lead a race is to be first

explanation.surface: The pigsty was the first thing on the farm to be planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Styled means given a particular shape or look, fashioned deliberately, so it means designed.

clue.text: Irritation in places about unfair arrangement

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for places runs backwards
in sets the first word inside the other

blocks.note: to place something is to put it
an itch is an irritation

explanation.surface: An itchy rash in certain spots is a sign of something being wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: A stitch-up is British slang for a frame or rigged deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch-up is British slang for a rigged outcome or frame, an arrangement designed to cheat someone.
